clue.text: Lively riptides at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of riptides are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Strong currents in the ocean make for an exciting swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like part of the ocean picture but tells you to rearrange RIPTIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spirited is full of energy and courage, a close synonym of lively.

clue.text: Inn with litre is here? Not English, according to one putting out book!

parts.note: an inn is a pub
taken as written

indicators.note: 'Not English' asks for the English letter to be left out of the word next to it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pub with a litre on offer is nearby, then a non-English book-trade person answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' with 'English' is an instruction to drop the E; the question mark and exclamation dress the clue as a chatty sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm or person issuing books for sale is exactly what this trade name describes.

clue.text: After closure of bar, I was first to get angry

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter, so take the end of bar

parts.note: taken as written
to have led is to have been in first place

explanation.surface: Once the pub shut, someone was the first to lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closure of bar' sounds like closing time but gives only the last letter of bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means irritated or annoyed, a synonym for angry.

clue.text: Like meal that may have been cooked by scouter here

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been prepared and transformed, so the letters of scouter here are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Scout leader suggests the dinner they made at camp was a proper sit-down feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' belongs to the kitchen scene but is the anagram signal for SCOUTERHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal with starter, main and dessert is described as having that many stages.

clue.text: Dress up as duke, man, if being entertained

indicators.note: something entertained is taken in as a guest, so the word if goes inside the man's name

parts.note: Andy is a man's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man wonders whether to dress up as a duke if invited to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being entertained' is a containment signal: the man hosts the word 'if' as a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: To dandify is to make smart or foppish in appearance, as a dandy would be.

clue.text: Not liking the effect of a cold day in place of business

parts.note: to be off something is to have gone off it, no longer liking it

parts.words: the effect of a cold day
parts.note: ice forms when the weather is freezing

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the way a chilly day affects their workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a room or building where work and administration are done.

clue.text: Bird to 'oller?

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a bird makes a noise to holler, in a dropped-h accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'oller is a hint that the verb meaning to holler should lose its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a nocturnal hooting raptor; and to holler, with the h dropped in Cockney style, is to howl without its first letter.

clue.text: Float with glee when this instrument is played

definitions.text: Float with glee when this instrument is played

indicators.note: playing an instrument works the notes into a tune, so the letters of float and glee are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A carnival float rolls along to music played joyfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the instrument and shuffles FLOAT and GLEE, signalled by 'when this instrument is played'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small woodwind pipe, a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Basket with a hundred fish across the river

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the hundred and the fish sit either side of the river letter

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
an eel is a fish
R is a standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An angler's basket holds a hundred fish caught on the far bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts R between C and EEL. A creel is the wicker basket anglers carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker container used by anglers for their catch.

clue.text: One man was murdered, and another by lake

parts.note: another man, here Abe, a short form of Abraham

explanation.surface: One man is killed, and a second is found near the water.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Cain murders his brother, the first killing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this son of Adam is slain by his brother Cain, the first murder victim.

clue.text: Operatic cycle with songs heard from firebrand

parts.note: Wagner's Ring is a cycle of four operas

indicators.note: something heard is spoken, so the word for songs is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: lieder are German art songs

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser's voice is heard singing songs from Wagner's operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns LIEDER (German songs) into its soundalike, so RING + LEADER.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand stirs others to trouble, which is what an instigator of a revolt does.

clue.text: Theologian placed in official record as cheat

indicators.note: something placed in another is put inside it, so the theologian's letters go into the record

parts.note: a file is an official record kept on someone
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the degree of a theologian

explanation.surface: A theologian's name appears in an official dossier as a fraudster.
explanation.walkthrough: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, the classic crossword theologian; 'placed in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to swindle or falsify, a synonym for cheat.

clue.text: Lives in Somerset city, independent at the outset

parts.note: Ind is an abbreviation for independent, placed at the outset of the answer
Wells is a small cathedral city in Somerset

explanation.surface: Someone lives in a Somerset city and has been independent from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: WELLS is England's smallest city, in the county of Somerset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To indwell is to dwell inside or inhabit, so the verb means lives in.

clue.text: Incomprehensible language from wife after a big drink

indicators.note: 'after' puts the wife's word following the drink in the answer

parts.note: a double is a twice-sized measure of spirits
'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife

explanation.surface: After a stiff drink, a husband's wife speaks nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: DUTCH for wife comes from Cockney London slang, 'my old Dutch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Double Dutch is the idiom for gibberish or speech nobody can follow.

clue.text: No house may get renovated? There's expression of disapproval

indicators.note: a building that is renovated is reworked, so the letters of No house may are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A council bans home improvements, prompting public tutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' belongs to the fodder, not the sentence; 'get renovated' rearranges NOHOUSEMAY.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the idiom one uses to scold someone for bad behaviour, a reproach.

clue.text: Thinks friends should accept change

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the friends' word goes round the change

parts.note: mates are friends
to edit is to change a text

explanation.surface: Someone muses that their pals ought to embrace new ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should accept' is a containment signal; 'change' looks like part of the advice but is a verb meaning edit.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect or ponder deeply, so it means thinks.

clue.text: Strip of wood machine cut short

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter of the machine goes

parts.note: a lathe is a machine for turning wood or metal

explanation.surface: A thin piece of timber is trimmed by a woodworking machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the final E of LATHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lath is a thin flat batten, as used behind plaster.

clue.text: Nag who could make man target

indicators.note: letters that could make another word are reassembled, so man target is rearranged

explanation.surface: A scold may turn a man into a target for her complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' is the anagram signal for MANTARGET.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is an overbearing, scolding woman, which is what nag means as a noun.

clue.text: Man making female embarrassed

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: A chap makes a woman blush.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred is a common male first name, so it is a man.

clue.text: A Conservative backing the party making disclosure

indicators.note: 'backing' means coming behind, so the A and the Conservative follow the party in the answer

parts.note: a revel is a lively party
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory supports the party, which leads to a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for a political party, but it signals that the Conservative comes behind the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelatory describes something that reveals or uncovers hidden facts.

clue.text: Appearances made by twice the normal number of wise men

parts.note: the Magi are traditionally three, so twice that is six, VI in Roman numerals
sages are wise men

explanation.surface: A nativity scene shows double the usual crowd of wise men.
explanation.walkthrough: The Christmas story has three wise men, so 'twice the normal number' is six, written VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Visages are faces, the looks or appearances people present.

clue.text: Locks originally for stronghold

indicators.note: 'originally' places the word for at the start, ahead of the locks

parts.note: taken as written
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Locks, at first, were for a castle's defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' puts the word for first; 'Locks' looks like door fittings but means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress is a fortified building, a defensive stronghold.

clue.text: Arab oil running short around island

indicators.note: 'around' puts the remaining letters of oil either side of the island
running short of something means one is missing it, here the last letter of oil

parts.note: the Isle of Man is often just Man in crosswords

explanation.surface: An Arab state's oil supply is dwindling near an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running short' cuts the L from oil, leaving OI, which goes 'around' MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Oman on the Arabian peninsula is an Arab.

clue.text: Pay journalist back, having brawl

indicators.note: 'back' tells you to read the journalist's letters the other way round

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a crossword journalist
a fray is a fight or brawl

explanation.surface: A reporter is paid back after getting into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: ED, for editor, is the stock crossword journalist; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay for them.

clue.text: Place of discussion suitable for children in class

indicators.note: 'in' puts the children's rating inside the class

parts.note: a form is a school class in Britain
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, fine for children

explanation.surface: A classroom debate is designed for young pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all ages; FORM is a British school class or year.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a venue or medium for public debate.

clue.text: Maker of wagon — vehicle used by couple not quite acceptable

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so the last letter of the couple's number is dropped

parts.note: a couple is two
right means proper or acceptable

explanation.surface: A carriage builder is told a vehicle used by two people isn't quite up to standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of the couple's number; a wright is an old word for a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A wright is a maker, so this craftsman builds carts and wagons.

clue.text: Grass twisted the wrong way, they say

indicators.note: 'they say' signals that the word is replaced by one spoken the same way

parts.note: wry means bent or twisted to one side

explanation.surface: A blade of grass is bent awry, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' sounds WRY as the cereal grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal plant, a member of the grass family.

clue.text: Actual field maiden's got lost in

indicators.note: something that has got lost in a place has vanished from it, so the maiden's letter goes

parts.note: a realm is a field or domain of activity
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman really did go missing in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: Real means existing in fact, which is what actual means.

clue.text: The children he abandoned may feature in the paper

indicators.note: what is abandoned is left behind, so the letters of he are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
issue means offspring or children
taken as written

explanation.surface: A father who left his family might appear in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops HE from THE ISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is fine thin paper, used for wrapping or as a handkerchief.

clue.text: Plans to hold various matches in south Africa

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so south Africa's letters wrap the mixed-up matches

parts.note: S for south and A for Africa

indicators.note: various means assorted, so the letters of matches are rearranged

parts.note: the printed fodder word; the setter's anagram needs six letters here, M A T C H E, to fit between S and A

explanation.surface: Organisers plan to stage several matches in the south of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: SA must 'hold' an anagram, but all seven letters of MATCHES would make nine; only MATCHE fits, giving S CHEMAT A.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemata are outlines or diagrammatic plans, the plural of schema.
